name: Park and Activities Commission Adjourned Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MAY 20, 2025

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 6:09 p.m. at George F Canyon Nature Center, 27305 Palos
  Verdes Dr. E, Rolling Hills Estates, California, by VICE CHAIR POPE.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  VICE CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla,  Holdsworth,  Bain,  and
  McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  Persichina

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF APRIL 15,
  2025

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  APRIL 15, 2025.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND PRESERVE ANNUAL REPORT
  2024

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
May 20, 2025
   Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy (PVPLC) Education Director Holly
  Gray gave an overview of the George F Canyon Nature Center and Preserve
  annual report (as per the agenda materials).

  Ms. Gray clarified that field trip participant numbers were slightly lower than
  previous years as the PVPLC has limited field trip group size to 20-25 children due
  to the limited restroom facilities and spaces to accommodate the groups, in
  response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK.

  Discussion ensued regarding the current closed condition of the Nature Center
  structure and the future Nature Center project exhibits.

  B.  STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION PROGRAM REQUEST FROM
  ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB ESTATES HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATON

  Superintendent Goldsmith gave a brief overview of the beautification request from
  the Rolling Hills Country Club Estates Homeowners Association (as per the
  agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER BAIN inquired about the Rolling Hills Estates Country Club
  Estates Homeowners Association’s (RHECC HOA) decision to change the tree
  from a Magnolia Tree to an Olive Tree. RHECC HOA Board Member John Alvin
  stated that the landscaper suggested going with an Olive Tree as it is not as
  invasive as a Magnolia Tree. He added that the Olive Tree would be a miniature
  of the standard Olive Tree and would not bear fruit. Superintendent Goldsmith
  noted that Olive Trees can be treated prior to the trees blooming to prevent them
  from bearing fruit.

  VICE CHAIR POPE asked about aspects of the sign, including the color, and
  whether other signs in the City also lacked a white background. Mr. Alvin noted
  that RHECC is looking at a dark brown color for the sign. Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated that there are other neighborhoods that have entryway signs that
  do not have a white background. Mr. Alvin stated there is other neighborhood
  entryway signs that have a dark brown/standard brown color.

  A discussion ensued between Mr. Alvin and Staff regarding the completion timeline
  of the entryway project.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  HOLDSWORTH to:

  APPROVE THE CHANGES TO THE ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB
  ESTATES HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION’S ORIGINAL REQUEST
  APPROVED ON JANUARY 21, 2025, GRANTING $2,500 IN MATCHING
  FUNDS FROM THE CITY’S STREET ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION
  PROGAM IN FY 2024-2025.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
May 20, 2025
   AYES:  Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, Bain, McCormick, Pope
  ABSENT:  Persichina

  C.  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the Peninsula Holiday Parade
  Management Services for the upcoming 2025 parade (as per the agenda
  material).

  In response to VICE CHAIR POPE, Supervisor Pinuelas clarified that there were
  some challenges with the previous parade contractor and Staff felt that it would be
  best to proceed with a different contractor. She also noted that Staff met with the
  proposed parade contractor, provided a list of what Staff needed and have been
  pleased with their responses and experience with other parades and similar
  events.

  In response to COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK, Supervisor Pinuelas noted that
  the same scope of services was provided for this proposal, the services provided
  by the parade management contractor and City staff would be similar to that of
  previous parades.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  HOLDSWORTH to:

  RECOMMEND TO CITY COUNCIL TO PROCEED WITH BELL EVENT
  SERVICES, INC. TO PROVIDE PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES
  FOR THE PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE ON DECEMBER 6, 2025.

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth, Bain, McCormick, Pope
  ABSENT:  Persichina

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  MAYOR’S RIDE DEBRIEF (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided a debrief regarding the Mayor’s Ride event held on
  Saturday, May 10. He shared that multiple equestrian groups that participated in
  the ride and the attendance at the Scout Pancake Breakfast portion of the event
  at Ernie Howlett Park.

  B.  HILLS ARE ALIVE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided an update regarding the upcoming Hills Are Alive
  5k/10k event on Saturday, May 31. He provided information regarding registration
  numbers, sponsorships and volunteers.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
May 20, 2025
   C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.
  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK provided an update regarding the George F
  Canyon Preserve and Trail. He noted that everything looked good, but that there
  were some spots on the trail that needed to be cleaned up due to some overgrowth
  and weeds. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he would have Maintenance
  staff take a look, trim back and clean up the areas.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK inquired about the current status of the City
  Manager park video series posed on the City’s social media accounts. Supervisor
  Pinuelas stated that she would check to see if the videos were still in rotation.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about promotion of the Pepper Tree
  Foundation and if the special projects funded by the Pepper Tree Foundation were
  getting recognition via the City’s social media accounts. Supervisor Pinuelas
  affirmed.

  VICE CHAIR POPE stated that one of the City signs at the entrance to the City
  limits near the Rolling Hills Country Club was starting to deteriorate.
  Superintendent Goldsmith noted that he started taking inventory of those signs and
  would check that one and repair it as necessary. VICE CHAIR POPE also shared
  that she attended the last City Council meeting during which the Council approved
  the Military Banner Program.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that there was a tree in her neighborhood that
  appeared to have a very low hanging branch that may need to be trimming.
  Superintendent Goldsmith said he would investigate and see if it was a City tree.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF APRIL 22, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  PARK TOURS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
May 20, 2025
   A.  GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER AND PRESERVE/TRAIL,
  DAPPLEGRAY PARK, FOUNDERS PARK, AND TABER GROVE

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the George F Canyon Nature Center
  Project Update (as per the agenda materials).

  Discussion ensued regarding a potential need for longer-term temporary service
  for the Center’s programs, consideration for long-term plans to protect the closed
  building, and the potential to promote project fundraising opportunities at the site
  through PVPLC plant sales and other similar events held there.

  The Commission and Staff discussed that the parks were in good condition with
  nothing of notable interest to report on or view. The Commission decided to forgo
  tours of the parks listed.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

  VICE CHAIR POPE ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:01 PM TO THE NEXT
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JUNE 17, 2025, AT 6:00
  P.M., WHICH WILL BE HELD AT ERNIE HOLWETT PARK.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  ___________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Lisa Van Ingen Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Vice Chair, Park & Activities
  Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  5
May 20, 2025
